challenges.name: tool-calling-who-decides
challenges.title: Tool calling: who decides what runs?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the AI tutor: the trace of the getSubmission incident with the fix that followed, and a handler that trusts the JSON Schema it sent to the model.

questions.explanation: True. After the fix the handler reads the user from the authenticated session, so the userId value the model wrote is never used: the replayed call reads u_1047's own submission or nothing. The system prompt plays no part in that decision any more, which is the point: a pasted message can change what the model proposes, it cannot change what the server code does with the session. A complete gate also rejects the extra userId argument so the attempt shows up in the logs, but even without that, the data leak is closed. The common misconception is that the fix for a prompt injection is a stricter prompt; the fix is to take the decision away from the model.

False. The schema is sent to the model as part of the request: it guides what the model writes, and whether a provider enforces it depends on the provider, the model and the mode you asked for (some offer a strict or constrained mode; check the current documentation). The gateway may also fall back to another provider, and fakes and recorded fixtures contain whatever they contain. At runtime the cast checks nothing: {"courseId":"sql-basics","limit":"5"}, a limit of 500, a missing courseId or truncated JSON all reach listSubmissions. Parse the text as unknown and validate it against the same rules on the server. The misconception is that describing a shape to the model is the same as validating it.

challenges.name: tool-call-gate
challenges.title: The tool gate: check every proposed call before it runs
challenges.description:
The CodeDev AI tutor lets the model propose tool calls; this gate decides which ones run. Incident: getSubmission took a userId argument from the model, and a pasted prompt made the tutor read learner u_2291's code for learner u_1047. Write checkToolCalls(input). Input: { sessionUserId, confirmedCallIds, tools, calls }. A tool is { name, permission: "read-only" | "needs-confirmation", scope: "user" | "public", parameters }, where parameters maps each argument name to { type: "string" | "integer" | "boolean", required, minimum?, maximum?, maxLength?, enum? }. A proposed call is { id, name, arguments }, where arguments is the raw JSON text the model produced. Return one decision per call, in the same order: { id, tool, status: "run", args } or { id, tool, status: "rejected", reason }, where tool is the proposed name. Check in this order; the first failure gives the reason: (1) no tool has exactly that name: unknown tool "". (2) JSON.parse throws: arguments are not valid JSON. (3) the value is not a plain object (null, an array, a string or a number): arguments must be a JSON object. (4) it has an own property userId, with any value, even the session's: userId comes from the session. (5) the first of its own keys, in key order, that is not an own key of parameters: unexpected argument "" (inherited names such as constructor or toString are not parameters). (6) each parameter, in the order of parameters: absent and required gives missing argument "

" (absent and optional is skipped; null counts as present with a wrong type); an integer must be a number for which Number.isInteger is true, else argument "

" must be integer, and below minimum or above maximum gives argument "

" is out of range; a string must be a string, else argument "

" must be string, then longer than maxLength gives argument "

" is too long, then a value not in enum (exact, case-sensitive) gives argument "

" is not an allowed value; a boolean must be true or false, else argument "

" must be boolean. (7) a needs-confirmation tool whose call id is not in confirmedCallIds: needs confirmation. Otherwise the call runs with args = a new object holding only the declared parameters that were given, plus userId = sessionUserId when the tool's scope is "user" (key order inside args does not matter). The runner reads one input and prints the list of decisions as JSON.
hints: For a single proposed call, which question has to be answered before any other question even makes sense? Write the checks as a list in that order, and let the first failing one produce the reason.

Look at four places: a Map from tool name to definition; JSON.parse inside try/catch with the result typed unknown; a plain-object check (typeof, null, Array.isArray) before you read any key; and Object.hasOwn(obj, key), both for "did the model send userId" and for "is this key a declared parameter" - the in operator also finds inherited names such as constructor. Build args as a fresh object while you check each parameter, and add userId last.

A similar gate on different data: a scheduleReminder tool (needs-confirmation, scope user) with minutes (integer, required, 5 to 120) and note (string, optional, maxLength 20). Trace: '{"minutes":"30"}' -> argument "minutes" must be integer. '{"minutes":30,"channel":"sms"}' -> unexpected argument "channel" (found before any parameter is checked). '{"minutes":3}' -> argument "minutes" is out of range. '{"minutes":30}' not confirmed -> needs confirmation; confirmed -> run with { minutes: 30, userId: <the session's id> }.
